thread:
amy (AMY Sales): Quick sync for the ACME POC. Customer requirement: private deployment with no public internet egress from their VPC. They want guidance: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering, exact firewall rule snippets we can hand them, implications if they do TLS inspection, and a rough POC cost estimate for 2 weeks (~5k req/day, ~50GB/day). @lina @devon @sanjay

lina (Solutions Eng): TL;DR: Both options are valid. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is simpler for a restrictive firewall because it only requires outbound to our ENIs and SGs. VPC Peering exposes L3 connectivity so it's more flexible (you can reach multiple subnets), but requires careful route table management and stricter IAM/ACL controls to avoid unintended access. PrivateLink tends to be easier for security reviews.

devon (Network Eng): Network notes: If they need source-IP preservation for their logging/IDS, VPC Peering + internal NAT/proxy keeps original client IPs available. PrivateLink will NAT at our ENIs so their downstream systems will see our ENI IPs (we can document that). For peering across AWS accounts, ensure both sides accept peering and update route tables; no transitive routing. I can provide per-region ENI CIDR ranges for the POC so they can add firewall rules.

sanjay (Security): TLS inspection: If customer wants to perform TLS MITM, that must happen entirely on their side (in front of the connections to our endpoints). For end-to-end confidentiality, they can use mTLS so inspection isn't possible/needed. For regulated workloads (PCI/HIPAA) we recommend end-to-end TLS and client certs; if they insist on inspecting, they must accept the compliance implications. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and can do mTLS with client cert rotation.

amy (AMY Sales): Pricing question: Will PrivateLink cause extra infra egress charges and does Redwood bill extra for that? They expect ~50GB/day for the POC and want a simple ballpark.

lina (Solutions Eng): Pricing split: (1) Cloud infra costs (charged by AWS/GCP) such as Interface Endpoint hourly charges and data processed charges are billed by the cloud and typically borne by the customer. (2) Redwood platform fees (Private deployment license / support) are billed by Redwood. For short POCs we can often cover the cloud infra costs with credits—ask sales-ops. I'll prepare a one-page POC estimate with both gross and net cost lines. :memo:

devon (Network Eng): Helpful firewall snippet customers can copy: 

```
# Example outbound rules for PrivateLink consumer
# Allow outbound HTTPS to Redwood PrivateLink ENIs (we will provide exact CIDRs)
ALLOW TCP 443 to 10.240.40.0/26    # REDWOOD-ENI-EAST-1 (example)
# If they choose VPC Peering and our egress requires NAT
ALLOW TCP 443 to 52.210.120.0/24   # REDWOOD-EGRESS-NAT (example)
# If routing via corporate proxy
ALLOW TCP 3128 to proxy.corp.internal (proxy IPs)
# DNS resolution
ALLOW UDP 53 to 10.0.0.2 (internal DNS)
```

devon (Network Eng): Note: if they use TLS inspection that strips SNI, host-based routing breaks. Recommend preserving SNI or deploy an L7 proxy that can route after decryption. If they cannot preserve SNI, we can provide a single hostname endpoint as a fallback but that reduces multi-tenant routing granularity.

sanjay (Security): Security bundle checklist I'll provide:
- SOC2 Type II report (latest)
- POC-specific data flow diagram (we'll mark ingress/egress and storage)
- KMS/HSM support doc (how to provide KMS ARNs and key policies)
- TLS and mTLS options, cert rotation cadence
- Pen-test summary and vulnerability disclosure contact
I'll upload these to the shared drive; turnaround ~2-3 business days for the full bundle.

amy (AMY Sales): I'll ask the customer to confirm: 1) PrivateLink or Peering preference, 2) whether they'll do TLS inspection, 3) need for source-IP preservation, 4) fill out the draft security questionnaire. Also will ask finance to pre-approve infra credits for the POC.

lina (Solutions Eng): Action items: I'll produce two small network diagrams (PrivateLink vs Peering) and the POC pricing sheet. devon: please provide the exact ENI CIDR ranges per-region and a minimal Terraform sample for the consumer. sanjay: please assemble the security bundle and KMS notes.

devon (Network Eng): I'll add ENI CIDRs and an IaC snippet for PrivateLink consumer setup. Example Terraform snippet: 

```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_private" {
  vpc_id            = var.customer_vpc_id
  service_name      = "com.redwood.inference.private"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.allow_redwood.id]
}
```

devon (Network Eng): Filing a short checklist for ops handoff: provide ENI CIDRs, indicate whether we need static egress NAT ranges, confirm DNS hostnames to use, and note any cross-account role ARNs for peering.

sanjay (Security): Timeline: If customer returns questionnaire today we can assemble the security bundle in ~3 business days. For KMS integration we'll need their KMS ARN and key policy during onboarding.

amy (AMY Sales): Main POC blocker for procurement: they want assurance against surprise egress charges. lina, call out a clear network-cost note and include sales-ops contact to request infra credits. I'll confirm POC SLA expectations in my next buyer email. :thumbsup:
